2. The plaintiff petitioner filed Title Suit No.84 of 1992 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar Court, Feni against the defendant respondents for declaration of title of the suit land. The plaintiffs case, in short, is that the land situated in Mouza No.75 Podua, pertaining Sabek Khatian No.74, Plot No.575 measuring 225 decimals of land originally belonged to Abdul Hakim Bhuiyan. He while in possession sold 22 decimals of land to Kala Mia, father of the plaintiff, by executing a registered deed of sale on 28.11.1921. After the death of Kala Mia, plaintiff along with his four sisters inherited the same and subsequently the plaintiff became the sole owner of the suit land by way of gift from his sisters. The plaintiff subsequently amended the plaint on 11.9.1994 claiming that the land under Khatian No. 9, Plot No. 394 measuring 5.14 acres was originally owned by Raja Birendra Kishor Manik, Raja of Tripura, who sold the same to Kala Mia and three others namely, Ajmat Ali Bhuiyan, Alim Uddin and Ashraf Ali by executing a registered deed of patta on 8.11.1919 and 10.11.1919 respectively. By virtue of the aforesaid transfer, father of the plaintiff acquired 1.28 acres of land in the said schedule out of total 5.14 acres of land. Subsequently Kala Mia and his co-sharer transferred 38 decimals of land by executing a registered patta on 29.10.1920 in favour of Abdul Aziz and Abdul Gani. After the aforesaid transfer, Kala Mia retained 1.19 acres of land out of 5.14 decimals of land and same was inherited by the plaintiff and his four sisters after the death of Kala Mia. Land inherited by his sisters was transferred in favour of the plaintiff by way of registered sale deed on 1.7.1975. In this way plaintiff became 16 annas owner of the suit land. Further case of the plaintiff is that Ali Azzam, father of the defendant No.1, was an uncle of the plaintiff. The plaintiff being a Government servant, served at different places in the country on transfer for which he kept the original deeds and the land to his uncle Ali Azzam to look after the property and to pay the rents. Accordingly Ali Azzam took the said deeds and the suit land and subsequently in collusion with the defendant No.10 recorded his name in respect of the suit land in the Government khatian (M.R. Khatian No.298). Further case of the plaintiff is that Ali Azzam retained the said deed till his death and he never returned the same to the plaintiff and after his death, the defendant No. 1 got the said deeds and refused to return the same to the plaintiff. The plaintiff later came to know that the suit land was recorded in the name of the predecessor of defendant Nos.1 and 2 which cast a cloud over the title of the plaintiff. Hence the suit. 

 3. The defendants contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable and barred by limitation. He further claimed that the suit land purchased by the father of the plaintiff by registered patta from the Raja of Tripura was in fact purchased in the benami of Ali Azzam who provided entire consideration for the said land and said fact was disclosed to the local salish which gave award in favour of Ali Azzam directing Kala Mia to transfer the land in Plot No.575 and Plot No.394 to Ali Azzam. Accordingly Kala Mia executed a sale deed in favour of Ali Azzam on 29.1.1948 by an unregistered deed. By virtue of the said transfer Ali Azzam became the owner of 86 decimals of land in both the schedules and was in possession of the same and neither Kala Mia nor the plaintiff was ever in possession of the suit land.
